title: Opening at Birdland, Roulette and playing opposite Basie
summary: They discuss Forrest's background; Edison recalls memorable nights at Morris Levy's Birdland.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about Jimmy Forrest. You knew him when you were in St. Louis?
Oh, yeah, I've been knowing him a long time, you know.
Jimmy, was he in that Jeter- Pillars band?
No, he didn't play in that band. He was with the Andy Kirk band.
Yeah, went to Andy Kirk. And -- but, oh, it was fantastic opening there at Birdland. And then I was signed with Roulette and all the Roulette artists were in Birdland all the time, anyway.
Yeah, Morris Levy's thing. And we would

play opposite Basie most of the time, you know. Basie would have a big band and I would have a small band. And we would -- oh, it was just absolutely -- such memorable nights we used to have down there, you know.
Well, that was when Birdland was really --

Oh, it was going then, yes. It was the only joint in New York to go to. That was the place after the 52nd Streets, after that. Because after 52nd Street, you know, the Birdland became the place to go, you know.
Then I had Elvin, he played with me two or three years.
